analysis.title: NVIDIA (NVDA): The China Problem
key_insights: Culper is short NVDA. It argues China still drove over 20% of FY2026 compute revenue through illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries, despite Nvidia saying its China business went to zero after the April 2025 restrictions.

Culper says documents suggest Alibaba secretly financed Megaspeed, Nvidia's largest Southeast Asian chip buyer, through apparent shell companies. Megaspeed is reportedly under investigation by U.S. Commerce and Singapore authorities. Nvidia's statement that Megaspeed has 'no China shareholders' covers equity ownership only, not financing.

Megaspeed's balance sheet grew from $33M to $3.0B in total liabilities and equity between year-end 2023 and 2024. The growth was driven by $2.9B of 'refundable deposits received' from an unnamed source and $2.9B of 'amounts due from subsidiaries'.

Malaysian filings show Speedmatrix pledged its entire business as collateral to Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) in June 2024, two months before it began operations. Apex's parent is Alibaba. As of 3/31/2025 Apex reported over $4.1B in prepayments against $4.2B in loans payable to Alibaba.

Trade records show Speedmatrix imported $4.6B of product from December 2024 to January 2026, of which $4.0B came from Aivres Systems, an Nvidia Elite OEM partner formerly named Inspur Systems. Aivres is one-third owned by the Chinese state, just under the 50% entity-list threshold. Culper calls it in effect a China-dedicated supply channel.

Giga Computing exported at least $511M of servers to Speedmatrix ($344M) and Novagate Cloud ($142M), including H200 and Blackwell Ultra B300 servers. Culper says Novagate looks like another Megaspeed affiliate, based on a near-identical website, a shared address and a Malaysian entity formed two days after the April 2025 restrictions.

Culper links the March 2026 DoJ Supermicro indictment ($2.5B smuggled via 'Company-1', reported by Bloomberg to be OBON Corp) to Megaspeed. It cites a former Nvidia employee calling Megaspeed 'just the tip of the iceberg' and says the OBON corridor is one of many.

Culper alleges Jensen Huang has a close relationship with Megaspeed's Alice Huang and visits Megaspeed-linked data centers with Alibaba representatives. These claims rest on anonymous sources, including a current Megaspeed employee. Nvidia's public position is that it found no diversion.

Culper says Nvidia's geographic reporting hides China exposure. Revenue is reported by customer headquarters location, and the October 2025 switch from billing location removed Singapore, which had grown from 8.5% of revenue in FY2023 to 20.1% for the LTM ended July 2025.

Culper says China is a downside risk, not upside. Beijing has blocked Nvidia imports in favor of domestic chips, trade records show lower CY Q1 2026 shipments, and Aivres appears to have shipped zero chips to Megaspeed in Q1 2026. Culper sees a large gap in FY2027/CY2026 estimates.

Third-party data cited: Chinese AI chip supply was about $12-13B in 2025 against a claimed $50B market. IDC put Nvidia's 2025 China share at 55% on about 2.2M cards. Culper estimates Nvidia sold only about 720,000 H20 cards that year.
Culper contrasts its view with the Street. Wells Fargo wrote in March 2026 that China could add $25B a year or more in incremental revenue, and Culper calls that backwards.

market_movers.rationale: Culper is short and says China revenue was never zero and is now actually going to zero. It sees a large gap in forward estimates and regulatory risk from diversion through Southeast Asia.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reported $19.7B of China revenue in FY2026, which Culper says reflects export controls taking effect partway through the year and non-data-center business such as gaming, networking and auto.

FY Q1 2026 H20 revenue was $4.6B before the new export licensing requirements. FY Q2 2026 included $650M of H20 sales to an unrestricted customer outside China, and the FY2026 10-K disclosed $60M of H20 revenue under U.S. government licenses. Culper puts CY2025 China H20 revenue at $7.15B at most.
Nvidia took a $5.5B H20 inventory write-down in April 2025 and guided to a loss of about $8B of H20 revenue in FY Q2 2026.
Culper says Wells Fargo's China upside implies $23-29B of FY2025 revenue and $39-48B of FY2026 revenue. Culper rejects this as a forecast basis.

trade_ideas.description: Short NVDA equity on China revenue exposure and diversion risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Culper says China revenue never went to zero, is now being cut by Beijing, and leaves a large gap in FY2027 estimates.

risk_factors: Regulatory and legal action over chip diversion, including the Commerce and Singapore investigations of Megaspeed and further DoJ cases.
Beijing's push for domestic chips could remove Nvidia's remaining China and Southeast Asian business.
The report relies heavily on anonymous source testimony, and its own disclaimer says opinions are not asserted as undisclosed facts.
Culper says it may trade in the securities at any time and will not update the report, so it has a short-seller conflict of interest.
Possible U.S. policy moves: Trump said in December 2025 that H200 sales to China would be allowed, though China is reportedly rejecting them.
SMCI and other OEM partners face exposure to smuggling cases.
geopolitical: The U.S. tightened export controls in April 2025, effectively banning Nvidia GPU sales to China.
The DoJ indicted three individuals tied to Supermicro in March 2026 over alleged smuggling of $2.5B of servers to China.
Megaspeed is reportedly under investigation by U.S. Commerce and Singapore authorities.

Beijing has blocked or discouraged Nvidia purchases: the CAC halted RTX Pro 6000D purchases in September 2025, customs crackdowns began in October 2025, and a ban on foreign AI chips in state-funded data centers was reported in November 2025. The FT reported H200 border blocks in January 2026.

Commerce Secretary Lutnick testified on April 22, 2026 that China has bought zero H200 chips. Senators Banks and Warren asked on March 23, 2026 for export licenses for China and Southeast Asian intermediaries to be paused.
The BIS 50%-ownership entity-list rule was issued in September 2025 and suspended for one year on November 10, 2025.
cross_bank_references: Wells Fargo wrote in March 2026 that 'China could drive $25B/annum+ in incremental revenue'.
DA Davidson's Gil Luria estimated in mid-2025 that 'at least 25%' of Nvidia chips and 'as much as 40%' of revenues reflect Chinese demand.
Wells Fargo noted that 'NVDA has previously noted that China accounted for 20-25% of total Data Center revenue.'

tension_points.bull_case: Analysts treat China as upside. Wells Fargo sees $25B or more a year in incremental revenue if trade relations improve. Nvidia says China fell to zero after April 2025 and that its spot checks found no diversion.
tension_points.bear_case: Culper says China never went to zero because of diversion via Southeast Asian intermediaries, and is now actually going to zero as Beijing blocks Nvidia chips. It sees a large gap in forward estimates and regulatory risk from the Megaspeed and Supermicro cases.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia producing evidence of a clean Megaspeed ownership and financing structure, or China permitting large H200 purchases. The report implies both but does not state a specific level or date.

theme_stances.key_argument: China drove over 20% of FY2026 compute revenue through diversion and intermediaries, and that business is now going to zero as Beijing blocks Nvidia chips.
theme_stances.evidence: Analysts treat China as potential upside. We believe it’s the exact opposite.
